rules.title: Ban on landlord use of algorithmic rent-setting devices (proposed SDMC Ch. 9, Art. 8, Div. 11)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not use an algorithmic device, meaning software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rents or occupancy levels, to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in San Diego. Each month and each property in violation counts as a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 civil penalty per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property in the City of San Diego, as defined in SDMC § 98.0702.
rules.exemptions: Software that publishes reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or from public information, and does not recommend rents or occupancy levels for future leases or renewals. Software used to set rents or income limits under local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where the software uses nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy levels. Affordable-housing-guideline software and aggregated reports using data more than 90 days old are excluded.

rules.penalty: Tenant civil action for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. A prevailing tenant recovers costs and reasonable attorney's fees. Remedies are cumulative, and Chapter 1, Article 2 SDMC enforcement remedies also apply.
rules.quoted_span: (b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.conflict_note: The document is a February 27, 2025 staff report and draft ordinance (O-2025-107). The ordinance number, date of final passage, and adoption date are all blank. It would take effect on the 30th day after final passage. This document does not confirm adoption as of 2026-10-01. Possible interaction with California state law on algorithmic pricing is not addressed.

rules.title: Ban on selling or licensing algorithmic rent-setting devices to landlords (proposed SDMC § 98.1103(a))
rules.requirement: No person may sell, license, or otherwise provide to a landlord an algorithmic device that uses nonpublic competitor data to advise on or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for San Diego residential rental property.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person providing algorithmic rent-setting software to landlords with respect to residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Aggregated reporting software using nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or public information, that does not recommend future rents or occupancy levels. Software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Depends on whether the software uses nonpublic competitor data to recommend rents or occupancy levels.

rules.penalty: Remedies under § 98.1104 and Chapter 1, Article 2 SDMC judicial and administrative enforcement.
rules.quoted_span: (a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.
rules.conflict_note: This is a draft ordinance with a blank passage date. It would take effect 30 days after final passage, but adoption is not confirmed by this document as of 2026-10-01.
